title: U9 TITANS RECEIVE SPORTSMANSHIP AWARD
author: Siobhan Kos-Hodge
summary: Linslade Galaxy side recognised in BMSL AGM
body:
In this evening’s BMSL AGM, there was some really positive news for our U9 Titans side who out of the 50 plus teams in their age group in the season just finished received the BMSL Sportsmanship Award.

U9 Titans scored an average of 9.84 out of 10 across the whole of the season.

The players, coaches and parents/carers can feel rightly proud of Titans as they continue to embody the values that make Linslade Galaxy special as a real fun and friendly Club.
Titans have received a £50 sports voucher for head Coach, Vishal, to spend on the team.

title: U15 SPARTAK IN PENALTIES DRAMA
author: Philip Stanley
summary: Heartbreak for Spartak after match finishes at 1-1
body:
MKDDL U15 League Cup Final
Buckingham u15 Wanderers 1-1 AET (7-6 pens) Linslade Galaxy u15 Spartak

The sun was beating down to make very hot conditions for the League Cup final against Buckingham.

Coach Steve had a full squad to choose from other than Elliot who was forced to play the role of unused sub due to injury.
In the end Spartak were left to rue their missed chances as heartbreak in the penalty shoot out meant that they couldn’t win a trophy for the second season in succession.

The match opened in frantic fashion. After 2 minutes Luke did well to intercept and fed Ethan in the box. However, his cross was met by the defence. Within the next 60 seconds both teams had a clear chance but Buckingham scuffed their shot and Ethan’s shot from a narrow angle was just about saved by the goalkeeper as it looked for a second it would squirm under him.

There were early chances galore when Jack R did well on right and his cross was met by Mathew. His shot was deflected high and the goalie had to scramble to pad the ball away.

Next was a marauding run after 10 from Luke but the final shot was weak and easy for the keeper. Just a minute later Tycho rose like a salmon to head the ball from a corner onto the crossbar.

In spurts the match was end to end. Buckingham had a shot after 16 minutes followed by another Ethan effort in the box but his left foot shot had no power. The next second the ball went all the way through but Caelan did enough to put the striker off.

At the first drinks break Spartak had been playing the better football and had edged the chances. Ethan had a number of chances which all fell on his left foot and Buckingham looked dangerous when they broke.

title: U15 SPARTAK WIN EDGE FC TOURNAMENT
author: Philip Stanley
summary:
Spartak finish season on a high by winning high quality event
(Many thanks to Coach, Steve, for the match report)
body:
Linslade Galaxy U-15 Spartak wrapped up what’s proved to have been a turbulent season on a high with Victory at the Edge Academy tournament at the weekend.

The boys played some great football throughout the day, finishing second in their group of six teams, to reach the gold cup semi finals. In the semi finals Spartak faced previously unbeaten Woody’s from Enfield and put in a top performance to progress to the final.

title: LINSLADE GALAXY FC 2026 AGM
author: Philip Stanley
summary:
All Club Members invited to our Annual General Meeting
The Linslade Galaxy FC Annual General Meeting (AGM) this year is to take place on 14th July 2025 (7 p.m.—9p.m.) at:
body:
The Hare (Public House)
10 Southcott Village
Leighton Buzzard
LU7 2PR

The AGM is open to all club members and is an important part of the annual progress of the Club. It is held to make decisions that affect what the Club does and how it is run.
The AGM will:
- Highlight the progress and achievements of the club over the past 12 months.
- Elect the Committee for the following year.
- Discuss and vote on any changes to the constitution.
- Produce (and review) the club's annual accounts.

As such please come along to this important meeting and have your say on how your Club is run.

title: U14 PORTO START SEASON WITH FULL EFFORT
author: Philip Stanley
summary: Depleted Galaxy dig in but fine margins go Brickhill's way!
body:
(Many thanks to Coach, Pedro, for the match report)

MKDDL U14 Division 2
Result: Brickhill Wanderers 2–0 Linslade Galaxy Porto

A long road trip to Bedford, a depleted squad, a stiff wind and an uneven surface — and Brickhill had the ball in the net inside the opening minutes, a goal that came from nowhere and rocked Galaxy before they'd had a chance to settle.

To their credit, the lads took the sting out of it and slowly grew into the contest. Brickhill leaned on their physical superiority with a direct, long-ball approach, but Galaxy's back line marshalled it well, and neither keeper was seriously tested across the 90.

The best moment of the first half fell to Galaxy. Stan fashioned a terrific opening for Jack, who couldn't quite apply the finish the move deserved. That one goes in and the complexion of the afternoon changes entirely. Tom then produced another fine passage, wriggling clear of two challenges to drive into the box, only for the final ball to escape him.

It stayed that way: a game of few clear-cut chances, with both defences on top. Galaxy probed for the equaliser and had further sights of it, but couldn't find that last step or the finish to get us back in it. Brickhill then settled it at the death with a second to seal the points.

Man of the Match: Fred — relentless effort and desire, leading the charge in midfield from first whistle to last.

Plenty to be positive about and improve, but against the odds the boys stuck at it, and they should be proud of the effort they put in. That effort and commitment will be crucial for the season ahead.

title: MEERKATS' NEW KIT FEATURED IN LOCAL NEWS
author: Leighton Buzzard Observer
summary: Linslade Galaxy Meerkats U9 Girls have been featured in the local press after receiving brand-new kits with support from Unite the Union.
body:
Linslade Galaxy Meerkats U9 Girls have been featured by the Leighton Buzzard Observer after receiving their first brand-new official kit in three years.

The new kit was provided with the support of Unite the Union's Bedfordshire and Hertfordshire District Branch, replacing the team's previous collection of mismatched hand-me-downs.

Assistant coach Jeff Hodge said the new kit had given the squad a real sense of pride and excitement ahead of the season.
